en: You decide to get up and look for him.
You haven't been able to find him anywhere nearby.
You hear stirring, and then the door opens and closes. You look up and see Nazar's bed is empty.
You heard something move. Someone else is nearby.
You suspect he's gone to relieve himself, but after a few long moments, he does not return, and a quick glance outside finds him nowhere near.
You take a moment to carefully climb over the fence and into the courtyard of the ruined building. Nazar must be in here somewhere.
This sign is very, very old.
It reads : The serpent slays with subtle strikes. No other is welcome here.
The pedestal is stained with crusted yellow ichor. There is an inscription on the very top.
Under this mattress is a knife. Who knows how long it's been here?
Most of these volumes appear to be idle distractions. There is one that is still in particularly good shape.
There is no fuel for this furnace.
"It's called "Sovereign Star". It's a song about remembering home, even when you're far away, and about being able to find your way back."
At times like these, it is easy to forget how close by the dangers of Lukatt really are.
The night is peaceful and your party rests soundly in the old schoolhouse.
You gather up your firewood and have your evening meal. The night is cool, but the fire is warm, and it promises to be an easy night.
A group of rough-looking men are drawing in on a woman with a heavy axe. It appears that she has been ambushed.
She takes a deep breath, and her face remains stony.

The woman is cleaning the blood off of herself using a rag she has torn from one of the mangled corpses. When she sees you approaching, she throws down the rag and grips her axe haft, anger glinting in her eyes.
There is a tense moment as she sizes you up, apparently deciding whether or not to do to you what she did to the men from earlier.
Without saying anything, the woman charges toward the man, her still-bloody axe trailing behind her.
The chest is locked with some sort of magical seal which appears to be opened only with a matching trinket.
There are various interesting literature and cookbooks on this bookshelf. Though none of them are particularly rare or useful enough to take.
There doesn't seem to be any keyholes that you can see or any magic that you can sense keeping the chest shut, but the lid just doesn't budge at all.
This chest appears to be locked with some complex mechanism. There doesn't appear to be any way to pick or otherwise bypass the lock.
You pull at a few books, and find that one of them is a trick book that cause the nearby doors to click.
At the bottom of this water-filled barrel is a dark object of some kind.
A cool, salty air wafts through the room, and a distinct vibration shudders through the floor.
An eerie, almost supernatural hush falls over the worship hall, as if the whole world is waiting for you to speak.
It is unmistakable. This is the same carving you saw in the undersea temple dedicated to Leviathan.
Nazar pulls you close and kisses you in a way that is slow and mighty and quite unlike any kiss you have shared before.
Nazar reaches into his pack, and pulls out a small bundle. His hands are still shaking as he begins to unwrap it, and he pulls it around your shoulders.
Nazar trembles as you reach around his waist and fasten the magnificent buckle around his hips. His gigantic hands gently grip you shoulders, as though he is afraid he might fall.
Nothing happened.
Perhaps he never will.
Read through the journal?
Something has changed.

The only words you can pick out are "Gloried... he... hear... voices... echo... love". 
Based on the setting, it appears to be of some religious importance.
There is an ancient journal here, its pages undisturbed for many long years. The writing is florid and refined, clearly the hand of educated nobility.
There is an elaborate relief-carved medallion in the floor here. The image shows a man enveloped in swirling water.
There is an inscription carved around the edges of the medallion, but whether due to age or vandalism, most of it is illegible.
There is another entry, written in a much less-careful hand. Would you like to read it?
Trembling, Nazar holds out his hand. Swallowing hard, he nods his head once, and carefully takes the ring, slipping it onto one of his gigantic fingers.
When the chill of the evening becomes too much to bear and you make ready to return to camp, Nazar holds your hand tightly, and seems to have forgotten how to let go.
You and Nazar waste away the twilight in each others' arms, pledging yourselves to one another, and whispering of your desires and your promises.
You raise your voice and try to recite the Sunken Prayer as you recall it.
You withdraw the treasure you prepared for him and present it to him, bowing low.
Some maps, like this one, cannot be secured. This means you won't discover any new travel destinations by coming here, and you can't make this location into a stronghold.
You can, however, use this map as a transit point between neighboring maps if you uncover multiple paths that connect it.
As you step into the area, a shriveled little creature notices you.
He takes a deep breath and looks around.
The guard ran off.
There is a small key tucked between two of the cut logs in this woodpile.
It reads : Prove that you have sacrificed in the pursuit of perfection.
The pedestal is marked with detailed carvings of diving birds of prey. There is an inscription on the very top.
Add a piece of rope to the pulley?
Eight more pieces should be enough.
Five more pieces should be enough.
Four more pieces should be enough.
Nine more pieces should be enough.
One more piece should be enough.
Ride the ferry across the rapids?
Seven more pieces should be enough.
Six more pieces should be enough.
The pulley still needs more rope before it will be safe to use.
The rope on the pulley system has been entirely replaced. You can now use it to cross the rapids!

This looks like a pulley designed to reel the ferry across the water. The rope is rotting and threadbare, but if you can replace it with something stronger, you should be able to get the ferry working.
Three more pieces should be enough.
Two more pieces should be enough.
You securely tie a length of tough rope to the pulley system.
barrod, you get keys
Beauregard takes a deep breath and looks into the statue's face solemnly.

There is a barely legible inscription at the base of this statue. 
It reads - "Lord Maxim Spartill".
A popular man, evidently.

There is a gloriously-presented nude sculpture. The subject is dashing and heroic, and the presentation is both indulgent and reverent. What little he is wearing is reminiscent of a high-ranking military uniform.
There is a hole in the ceiling of the cave here, where sunlight streams through. A small patch of greenery soaks up the light.
There is something amid the leaves, glinting in the sunlight.
A wonderful, sweet smell hits your nose. Could it be...?
At first, you think he might just be salivating, but soon it becomes apparent that he is casting some kind of spell.
Greening sighs a long, deep sigh and shakes his head.
He doesn't appear to hear you, his voice rising in a crescendo as he completes his spell.
He's almost in a trance, and he really wants that cake.
His eyes glint with a kind of desperate madness, and his lips begin to move.
It would seem that the combination has to be performed quickly. Do you want to have another try?

Pine Needle Tea -- 20$
Wholewheat Scone and Jam -- 45$
Toasted Club Sandwich -- 70$
Black Forest Gateau -- 9,995$
Slowly, and with great reverence, he lifts the cake out of the chest and holds it aloft like some kind of trophy.
The chest is fitted with an unusal, circular lock which lacks a keyhole. While playing with the lock, you notice that it can be rotated, and it emits a quiet clunking noise.
The chest is fitted with an unusual, circular lock which lacks a keyhole. While playing with the lock, you notice that it can be rotated, and it emits a quiet clunking noise.
The lock emits a loud clanking noise. You take a moment to try and memorize the combination.
The lock jumps outward a little, and the chest lid automatically pops open.
The sign reads "Rosewood Teahouse Menu" in bold calligraphy across the top.
The varnish on these tables has mostly flaked off, and the exposed wood is quite damp and mouldy. It is hard to imagine that they have been used recently.
There is a small scrap of paper hidden underneath one of legs on this bed.
This small sack is made of a soft, white and grey pelt. You pick it up loosen the tie, and see that it is filled with coins.
Would you like to take it?
You are unsure if this sign has been altered by vandals, or whether the gateau really is that good.
You get halfway through the instructions before the mechanism lets out a loud noise. Perhaps the locking mechanism reset itself.
You lift up the leg and slide the piece of paper out from underneath.
You take the note you found from under the bed and follow the instructions written on it.
You turn the lock in both directions by varying degrees for a while, but to no avail.
You unfold the note. There are a bunch of circles drawn on it, and each one has a curved arrow and a number written inside.
A later entry follows up.
In the back cover of this book, there is a key pressed into the paper.
Some pages are particularly worn. On them are some footnotes detailing the repeated incarceration of an orc named "Odluk".
The last entry you can find pertaining to Odluk reads as follows.
The letter is signed, "Lord Maxim Spartill".
There are a few items still strewn across this dressing table. A few of them appear to be valuable.
There is a folded note conspicuously tucked into this bookshelf.

There is a recently-added drawing on the bottom of a naked singing orc and a noblewoman with something leaking out of her ear. 

She looks very surprised.
There is a small book forgotten in the bottom corner of this chest. Reading material for the guard, perhaps.
This bookshelf has a few rotting books with dungeon records, including the names and transgressions of several residents.
This desk has a half-penned letter still resting on it.
This looks like duty rosters for the guard rotations. They haven't been opened in a very long time.

This signpost is very old. It reads, 
"Breathtaking harmony heard the isle over! Come and treat your ears to the Royal Seamen's Chorus, playing all week!"
This unassuming end table has stood forgotten for many years. When you open it, you find a key that has managed to escape the notice of looters. Until now, that is.
As you examine the broken lantern, a small length of golden metal tumbles out of it.
It looks as though someone tore the casing off of this node. There are wires spilling out of it, and there is a conspicuous gap in the golden circuitry inside. Something has clearly been removed.
It looks as though the connection pin you took from the lantern might fit into the gap in the circuitry.
Some kind of metallic pillar. It is tightly sealed.
Some kind of metallic pillar. It looks like someone has tried, unsuccessfully, to break into it.
There are some scraps of paper on this table, but nothing has any legible text on it.
There is a short length of rotted twine stuck between two of the boards on the top of this table. It is not worth taking.
There is an empty ceramic cup caked over with dust, but nothing else of note.
There is nothing else of interest in this end table.
This is a long-dry basin, perhaps for water or maybe to serve as a collection plate.
This lantern looks like it has been pried open, and does not appear to be in working order.
When you touch the pin to the circuitry, a strong shock jolts your fingers! You'll have to be more careful on your next attempt.
You carefully slot the pin into the gap on the circuitry and quickly snap your hand away as a powerful blast of electricity surges through the node! You can feel the structure humming with power!
You find a small book in the drawer. It has obviously been very well-used, and the cover is torn off.
It reads : There is no sting worse than that of Zosark. Prove you can endure it.
The pedestal is cluttered with flaking rust. There is an inscription on the very top.
A blast of superheated air stings your eyes and throws you off.
A quick search reveals an access panel and some inner mechanism.
A spray of burning hot oil sends you reeling. A lighter touch may be needed.
A wave of hot air floors you. Your eyebrows are long gone.
After a brief search, you locate some kind of mechanism in a panel on the side of this statue.
As before, you have found some kind of access panel on the statue that reveals a mechanism.
Everything inside this mechanism is piping hot, and you burned yourself. You'll have to be more careful and try again.
It just got a lot hotter in here.
It looks as though your tampering is having... side effects.
Searching the chest a second time, you find a small switch hidden under the lip.
The battery clicks into place and the fire jet shuts off.
The depleted battery you found looks like it would fit perfectly into the impression in this jackal's chest.
There is an unusual indentation in the chest of this jackal statue, but no sign of an exposed mechanism.
There was a surge of fuel and an explosion! You managed to suffer only minor burns.
There was nothing inside of this chest.
This mechanism is barely even hidden.
This statue also appears to have a mechanism inside.
You cut yourself on an unseen sharp edge.
You disconnect a pressure regulator, and the fire dies out.
You gently shut off the fuel valve.
You kink a fuel line, and hear something further inside the mechanism break.
You manage to choke off a fuel valve, and the fire stops.
You redirect the fuel into a hollow part of the statue, and the fires sputter out.
You search the statue, but find nothing of particular note.
You spot a panel on the floor that appears to be out of place. It offers access to some kind of mechanism.
You've hopelessly mangled whatever that mechanism was.
"And that's how you felt when you and I married, Rangda?"

"At least, we're told that it's supposed to be. In reality they just exploit our eagerness to make us work harder. Most women go through five or six husbands in their lives, because there's always someone a little better, a little stronger, someone with a bigger cock."
"By the time she is free of it, if she is ever free of it at all, she'll be a withered old woman, too stretched and spent to chase after her dried-out dreams."
"Even if she does love her husband, she's little more than a sacrifice on the altar of the orcish nation."
"Everybody would be celebrating except for the bride, of course. She puts on a smile for her family, but she is screaming inside, being signed away as little more than breeding stock."
"Hah! Don't make me laugh. I'd rather fall on my blade than spend another day with you, and I'm doing just fine here, thanks."
"He works hard his whole life to stand out in a sea of men who will probably never get to be fathers, so that just maybe, a woman will pick him. It's a huge success when it actually happens."

"How many years has it been? Seven? Nine? And you think I'd spend that time pining after the woman who threw me away and cost me everything? Well I'd say we're pretty well even now, so good job. I owe you nothing."
"However hard we work, we're nothing more than olives, to be chewed, pitted, and spat upon the floor. What a fool I was."
"I bet they were so happy. Orc men are always excited at their weddings. "I'm one of the lucky few", he thinks. "I'll get to have some babies"."
"I came to rescue you from this place! To free you from this prison so we could be together again!"
"I came to rescue you. To get you off of this damned island!"
"I can't go back Nazar, you know that! I've given up my entire life to come here for your sake!"
"I would suggest trying to make some friends. You will probably need them."
"It makes me sick."
"Just like how my whole life was stripped away to send me here for your sake, right? Way I see it, that makes us even, so I owe you nothing. I am years done with you, woman."
"Let's go. There's nothing important here."
"Let's go."
"Nazar! You are alive! I've been searching for you ever since I got here!"
"Nazar... I gave up everything! I threw it all away to come here and find you, so we could be together again!"
"No, but together-"

"Not with you. Not back to Tsarath. Out here, I earn everything I have, and my life is difficult, but it's fair and it's mine. I don't have a selfish, short-sighted wife who can cut it off at a moment's notice."
"Now leave. If I ever see you again, you're going to get another sword lesson. A very short one."
"Now what am I supposed to do?"
"Now, this is my campsite, so I'd appreciate it if you'd take your friends and leave me be. You're scaring off the game."
"Rangda? What the hell are you doing here? Couldn't keep yourself out of trouble I assume?"
"Rescue me? What makes you think I need rescuing? I've never been happier in my life."
"Six torches. This was a wedding celebration. An orcish one."

"So you could have what you want, of course. No "I'm sorry I made stupid decisions that utterly ruined you". You wagered my life, Rangda! You knew this would happen and you did it anyway! Did it even occur to you that I didn't miss you? That I was glad to be rid of the whole stupid farce?"
"So you managed to get yourself thrown away too, did you? You must have done something really bad this time. What do you want, Rangda?"
"So? You don't have a way off the island. Nobody does."
"Together my ass, Rangda! I'm going nowhere with you, now or ever. You've done enough damage to me already!"

"Was I too harsh? 
No, don't answer that, I don't actually care. 

Let's be off."
"Welcome to Lukatt, by the way. Here, you can do anything you want. No laws at all! Enjoy."
"What? But this place is a prison, and polluted with monsters besides."
"What? You don't want to leave?"
"You know that isn't true, Nazar. I loved you dearly. I still do."
"You shouldn't have come here, Rangda."
Someone has been camping here recently. The embers of this fire are still warm.
A chunk of blackened meat lies inside the cage. It would be easy enough to reach through the bars and take it...
A couple of slices look edible, but they are certainly past their prime.
A rusted iron key sits inside the bucket. Take a closer look?
A small paper tag is tied to the key with some string. The writing on it reads "grounds maintenance".
A small pouch has been left on the ground here. It feels light when you lift it up, but there are a couple of useful items inside.
After some winding, the crank locks into place.
Magic runes have been hastily painted on the floor here, and are outlined by lit candles. You feel subtle vibrations coming from the runes, and they make you feel somewhat light-headed.
On this stump is a folded-over piece of paper weighed down by a small rock.
One of the books is noticeably lighter than the others. Opening it up reveals a hollowed-out section which houses an ornate black key.
Take a look inside?
Take the key with you?
That is probably for the best.
That is probably for the best. You place the lid back on top of the crate.
The chest is set with a solid gold lock. However, the lock seems to have been fitted incorrectly -- it wobbles around in place. Try opening it?
The lid disintegrates as you go to close it, and simply crumbles away into the box.
The locking mechanism falls off, and the chest opens with ease. The lock itself looks valuable, and might be worth taking.
The wood comprising this chest is singed all over, and is finely coated in ash. Would you like to open it?
There is a funny smell inside this shed, and these crates appear to be the source...
There is moderate resistance when attempting to turn the crank.
These books are filled with magic runes and a handful of strange diagrams.
Would you like to read the note?
You can attempt to extinguish the candles if you wish.
You slide the lid off the topmost crate and see piles of quiche slices stuffed inside. This was apparently the groundkeepers' favourite.

A pamphlet catches your eye. It describes how this cult is centred around the worship of the great and powerful "Matthaxus". There aren't any useful details regarding just what Matthaxus is, but the praise in this print is deliriously overzealous.
Rosaline tosses her hair, obviously more relaxed now that the trouble has been dealt with.
She stares at the ceiling for a moment, apparently thinking about something.
This chest appears to be full of typical provisions for the commune.
This drawer has a key inside of it.
Inside the chest is a collection of badly-spoiled provisions. You do, however, find an unopened bottle of wine that should still be safe to consume.
This water is stagnant and murky, but you catch sight of something at the bottom.
It's probably best not to force the issue.
Rangda is unusually quiet this morning. She doesn't look like she slept very well.
She picks up on your looking at her almost immediately. She opens her mouth as if to speak, but is overtaken by a yawn instead, and averts her eyes.
